A .collapsible is a stack of <details> sections. The browser opens and closes them. Give every section the same name and only one stays open; omit it (or add expandable) so several can stay open. AutoInit() starts the JavaScript API on every .collapsible except those marked no-autoinit — a details list still works without it.

Headers are a flex row. Wrap the title in collapsible-header-content when you add extra items such as a badge so they sit before the expand icon. See Badges in Collapsibles. Add no-icon to hide the trailing chevron.

Use a unique name per list on the same page — a shared name exclusive-opens across every matching <details>.

Initialization

The IIFE bundle exposes Expressive.Collapsible. Call init when you want the open / close API or the callbacks. Expressive.AutoInit() does that for every .collapsible. 

document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function() {
  const elems = document.querySelectorAll('.collapsible');
  const instances = Expressive.Collapsible.init(elems, {
    // specify options here
  });
});

Per-instance options can also be passed through AutoInit:

Expressive.AutoInit(document.body, {
  Collapsible: { accordion: true }
});
Preselected Section

Add the open attribute to the section that should start expanded. In accordion mode only the first open section stays that way; with expandable every open section stays open.

Options

You can customize each instance. Callbacks receive the <details> (or the alias li) that opened or closed. Duration and easing are CSS — set --md-comp-collapsible-duration (default 500ms), --md-comp-collapsible-easing-open, and --md-comp-collapsible-easing-close (both a soft ease-in-out by default).

Name Type Default Description
accordion Boolean true When true, only one section stays open. When false, several can stay open. The expandable class is the markup switch and does not need a no-autoinit.
onOpenStart Function null Called before a section opens.
onOpenEnd Function null Called after a section finishes opening.
onCloseStart Function null Called before a section closes.
onCloseEnd Function null Called after a section finishes closing.

Methods

All methods are called on the plugin instance. You can get the instance like this: 
const instance = Expressive.Collapsible.getInstance(elem);
.open();

Open a collapsible section.

Integer: 0-based index of the section to open.

instance.open(3);
.close();

Close a collapsible section.

Integer: 0-based index of the section to close.

instance.close(3);
.destroy();

Destroy the plugin instance and tear down its event handlers.

instance.destroy();

Properties

Name Type Description
el Element The DOM element the plugin was initialized with.
options Object The options the instance was initialized with.

Collapsible Types

A collapsible can allow several sections to stay open, or only one at a time (accordion). Accordion is the default.

Accordion

This is the default. Opening one section closes the others. Same name on each <details> is enough; AutoInit also assigns a shared name when it is missing.

Expandable

Add expandable so several sections can stay open. Leave name off the details. No no-autoinit and no options object.

Popout

Add the popout class for the raised, inset look. Behavior is still accordion unless you also add expandable.

List alias

The older <ul> / .collapsible-header / .collapsible-body markup still works. Add active to an li to preselect it. JavaScript drives open and close on this anatomy — AutoInit() or Collapsible.init.
